To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) jointly scoring and selecting salient and novel sentences is not as effective as first scoring salience and then balancing salience and redundancy; and 2) by learning to select sentences that have higher novelty, we are able to create summaries that contain less redundancy and more diversity.

(i) redundancy aware models that jointly score and select sentences outperform the baselines, and (ii) redundancy reduction is more important than sentence salience in creating high quality summaries.
i) jointly scoring salience and redundancy is not the best approach for extractive summarization; ii) explicitly modeling diversity in a separate step improves the overall performance.
